tasks.title: Confirm canonical target identity
tasks.why_for_this_request: Every later task depends on an exact canonical target; BRD4 was resolved as O60885 (curated_table, confidence 0.95) and must be pinned before evidence tasks run.

tasks.title: TargetTherapeuticsAssessment (pre-design gate)
tasks.why_for_this_request: Before any design work for BRD4, the evidence-backed assessment must resolve identity/variant/disease/cell context, gather Open Targets-style disease, dependency, normal-tissue, binder/structure and E3 evidence, distinguish association from causality, and decide whether degradation is justified, uncertain or unsuitable. Design must not bypass identity, chemistry or therapeutic-window gates.
tasks.evidence_gate: verdict != degradation_unsuitable AND identity/chemistry/window gates not blocked

tasks.title: Target biology and disease context
tasks.why_for_this_request: For BRD4 the first investigation question is the disease/target biology (context not pre-recorded): establishing degradation rationale decides which evidence gates matter next.
tasks.evidence_gate: >=1 retrieved primary source on target role/disease
tasks.branch_trigger: indexed literature evidence retrieved (or explicitly none)

tasks.title: Binder/warhead landscape
tasks.why_for_this_request: BRD4 has 120 known binder(s) recorded; the first ligand question is which of those binders have a usable attachment vector and measured (non-demo) potency to serve as warheads.
tasks.evidence_gate: >=1 source-backed binder with attachment vector and measured potency
tasks.branch_trigger: binder set with attachment vectors; otherwise hypothetical exit vectors

tasks.title: E3 ligase feasibility and ranking
tasks.why_for_this_request: BRD4 has measured degradation precedent (CRBN (26 rows), FEM1B (7 rows), VHL (32 rows)) in the packaged context set; the E3 question is which recruiter to prefer for this target (ligand availability + cell-context expression), not whether one exists.
tasks.branch_on_fail: open_question: E3 ranking undecidable from packaged evidence
tasks.branch_trigger: measured precedent rows or explicit user E3 preference

tasks.title: Structural and ternary-complex readiness
tasks.why_for_this_request: Experimental structures exist for BRD4 (2OSS,3MXF,5T35); the structural question is whether a docking-ready site can be derived and ternary modeling exercised (in /design), not assumed.
tasks.evidence_gate: usable structure + chosen warhead/E3 attachment points
tasks.branch_on_fail: open_question: structure not usable for this pairing
tasks.branch_trigger: usable model located + attachment vectors defined

tasks.title: Linker and exit-vector feasibility
tasks.why_for_this_request: Only meaningful after a source-backed warhead with an explicit attachment vector exists (T2 pass); otherwise deferred — feasibility is never assumed.

tasks.title: Validation design and next commands
tasks.why_for_this_request: Closes the plan: define what /design will generate and what /report will summarize for BRD4, plus a discriminating validation protocol — without running any of it here.
tasks.evidence_gate: design only if T2 passed; otherwise open questions block design

request: what is BRD4 and why is it a PROTAC target?

summary: BRD4 (Bromodomain-containing protein 4) is a member of the BET family of proteins, which are involved in chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. It plays a crucial role in gene expression

answer: BRD4 (Bromodomain-containing protein 4) is a member of the BET family of proteins, which are involved in chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. It plays a crucial role in gene expression by binding to acetylated histones and recruiting other transcription factors. BRD4 has been identified as a potential therapeutic target for various diseases, including cancer, due to its involvement in oncogenic signaling pathways. PROTACs targeting BRD4 can induce its degradation, thereby disrupting these pathways and potentially leading to cell death or inhibition of disease progression.
